text: 🎬 'Clayface' gets bloody in Gotham, but /Film finds no shape in it James Watkins , who made 'Eden Lake' and 'Speak No Evil', gives DC an R-rated body-horror spin-off. /Film says the gore is there but the film has no personality of its own. That's the risk with villain solo movies. After 'Joker', a bleak tone only works when it belongs to someone. Blood alone doesn't make a Gotham story distinct. Tom Rhys Harries has a transformation-heavy role, and Watkins knows how to build dread, so a limp result would point at the script. The cast also includes Naomi Ackie, Max Minghella, Eddie Marsan and Aaron Paul. ✈️ Add to watchlist

🎬 Apu speaks again on 'The Simpsons', and the voice is new Sunil Malhotra takes over Apu from Hank Azaria , who stepped away in 2017 after the backlash. The character returns in a Halloween episode, where Apu worries that Springfield has forgotten him. Homer sets him straight. Casting an Indian American actor fixes the problem that made Apu uncomfortable. It doesn't touch the older problem, which is the writing. 'The Simpsons' now has to give him jokes that aren't about the accent, and nine years of silence suggests the writers' room hasn't had many ideas. ✈️ Add to watchlist

🎬 Street Fighter won its weekend, but a sequel isn't a lock Kitao Sakurai 's 'Street Fighter' opened at No. 1 with $31 million domestic and $51.1 million worldwide. That is level with 'Masters of the Universe' and short of 'Mortal Kombat II' , which opened at $38.5 million. A start that size gets a sequel talked about, not signed. The budget, the overseas run and the film's second-weekend drop will decide it, and franchise fighting games have a bad record with follow-ups. Paramount's cast leans on Andrew Koji as Ryu, Noah Centineo as Ken, Callina Liang as Chun-Li, plus Jason Momoa and Roman Reigns. ✈️ Add to watchlist
